  • PURPOSE:

To provide guidelines for management of pain

  • SCOPE:

To provide pain management services to:

    • In-patients with acute and chronic pain related to terminal illness
    • In-patients with chronic pain related to chronic disease
    • Immediate post-operative patients
    • Patient needs pain management at the time of wound dressing
    • In-patient with angina and other cardiac problems
    • Out-patient with any orthopedic problems
  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Consultants
    • Anesthetist
    • Doctors
    • Nursing staff
    • Paramedical staff
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • COP: Care Of Patients
    • OPD: Out-Patient Department
  • DEFINITION:

NIL

  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: NABH Standards for Hospitals
  • POLICY & PROCEDURE:
    • Policy:
      • This hospital has a policy guide in the documentation of pain and its management depending on the severity of pain and it may be treated in a number of ways.
      • The policy of Hospital is to plan, support and coordinate activities and resources to ensure that the pain of all patients are recognized and addressed appropriately.
      • Patients with pain will undergo detailed assessment using pain rating scale and reassessed at appropriate intervals
      • Pain will be assessed and documented in the pain rating scale and patient education is provided on the same.
      • Pain alleviation measures or medications are initiated and titrated according to patient’s need and response.
      • The Hospital ensures pain management for treatment of such patients and availability of pain clinics in the OPD.
      • The pain clinic shall be conducted by the Anesthetist.
    • Screening, Assessment & Reassessment:
      • Screening:
        • All patients shall be screened for pain being the fifth vital sign.
        • Screening of pain is included in the ‘Initial Assessment Form’.
      • Assessment:
        • A detailed pain assessment is done when the pain is the predominant (or one of the main) symptom(s).
        • It shall be done for all postoperative patients.
        • The pain assessment includes:
        • Intensity of pain (can be done using a pain rating scale),
        • Pain character,
        • Acuity,
        • Location,
        • Modifying Factors
        • The assessment should be done in an objective manner so that it facilitates regular reassessment. For example, cancer pain, neuralgia and arthralgia.
        • This does not include chest pain due to angina or where the etiology of pain is physiological like labor pain.
        • Wong – Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale:

        • Simple Descriptive Pain Intensity Scale:

No pain Mild pain Moderate pain severe pain Very severe pain Worst possible pain

      • Re-Assessment:
        • Patients are reassessed for their pain at regular intervals as deemed necessary to see if their pain conditions have improved (pain reduction on numeric scale) so as to facilitate reduction of dosage of medications / frequency as appropriate.
        • Re-assessments are also done to ensure that there are no side effects post-administration of medication.
    • Pain alleviation measures:
      • Drug treatment:
        • Simple analgesics like Aspirin, Paracetamol, NSAID’s, anti-spasmodic and smooth muscle relaxants etc., or stronger medications like morphine to patients according to the doctor’s advice.
        • Stronger analgesics like morphine, methadone, codeine and similar narcotics are given only to inpatients under the close supervision of the treating doctor with the staff strictly following the narcotics protocol.
      • Nerve blocks:

By blocking a group of nerves with local anesthetics or blocking or destroying a ganglion with alcohol.

      • Physiotherapy:
        • Different exercises,
        • Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation,
        • Deep heat,
        • Ultrasound treatment,
        • Infra-red radiation,
        • Short wave diathermy,
        • Interference therapy,
        • Wax therapy,
        • Intermittent pelvic traction and intermittent cervical traction,
        • Electrical muscle stimulator etc. Are provided as and when indicated.
      • Psychological counseling
        • It is offered to patients suffering from chronic pain.
        • Some pain medicines are more effective in fighting pain when they are combined with other methods of treatment.
      • Titration of medication:
        • Based on the pain assessment and the underlying conditions, pain alleviation methods or medications are initiated for the patient.
        • Based on the patient response to the pain alleviation methods measures and medication are duly titrated
      • Nursing Care:
        • Monitor vital signs as ordered or as warranted. Assess the intensity, duration, and referred pain.
        • Implement measures to alter patient's perception of pain:
        • Administer prescribed analgesics.
        • Titrating medications, dosage, frequency within prescribed parameters (consult pharmacist on safe and effective parameters);
        • Offering non-invasive methods to alleviate discomfort (e.g., prayer, meditation, music, distraction, relaxation technique etc.).
        • Monitor the patient for side effects of analgesics and implement measures to combat or manage side effects (i.e., massage, vibration, routine bowel care, antiemetic, ointments, warm or cold therapy, exercise etc.).
        • Assess patient at regular intervals for:
        • Adequate pain control;
        • Bowel elimination;
        • Change in cognitive function;
        • General appearance and behavior;
        • Nutritional status.
        • Consult with physicians regarding Physical Therapy referral for:
        • Braces and splints as needed;
        • Assistive devices (walkers, canes, etc.)
        • Encourage patients and family participation in pain management regimen.
        • Notify treating physician of changes in patient or inadequate pain control.
      • Organization support:
        • The organization provides primary measures for immediate pain relief.
        • In case the hospital does not have facilities for further pain management it could refer such patients to centers specializing in pain management. Pain management includes medical, surgical and anesthetic techniques.
    • Patient Education:
      • The patient and his family are educated on the various pain management techniques.
      • Discuss with the patient and family probably physiological causes of pain that might be specific to patient (e.g., mass pressing on nerve, tumor obstructing bowel, etc.).
      • Teach the patient and family some non-invasive methods, which might help prevent or alleviate pain (e.g., distraction, music, reading, prayer, meditation, guided imagery, massage therapy, etc.).
      • Discuss with the patient and family the concepts of pain and pain management (e.g., reality of pain, variability and individuality of pain perception, etc.).
      • Discharge instruction regarding pain management.
      • Ensure that the discharge summary has the name & telephone number of the consultant to contact in case he / she has excessive discomfort.
